Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Acute diarrhea for approximately 3 days.
  - Frequency: 4–5 bowel movements per day.
  - Stool character: Varies by time of day; loose to watery at times.
  - Blood/mucus: Patient denies blood and mucus in stool.
  - Associated symptoms: Mild abdominal pain; one episode of vomiting; possible low-grade fever; decreased appetite.
  - Fluid intake: Patient reports drinking "plenty."
  - Recent exposures: No recent travel; no outside/dodgy food reported.
- Past medical history:
  - Asthma — patient states "probably had asthma" and "I guess I still have it" (current status uncertain).
- Medications:
  - "Lexapro" — dose/route/frequency not documented (patient states using a yellow inhaler and names this medication; clarification needed).
  - No other medications reported; no over-the-counter medications taken for current diarrhea.
- Social history:
  - No relevant travel or dietary exposures reported.
  - No tobacco/alcohol/drug history documented.
- Allergies:
  - Patient reports no known allergies.

Objective:
- General appearance/clinical observations:
  - Clinician noted patient appears not dehydrated.
  - Patient able to drink fluids.
- Gastrointestinal:

  - Reported one episode of vomiting.

  - No vital signs recorded in transcript.

  - No investigations performed or results available.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute diarrhoea:
   - Assessment or likely diagnosis: Acute diarrhoea.
   - Differential diagnosis:
     - Infectious gastroenteritis (viral or bacterial).
     - Food-related diarrhoea/intolerance.
   - Investigations planned:
     - Stool sample if diarrhea persists >1 week or if patient develops blood in stool.
   - Treatment planned:
     - Supportive care: oral hydration; consider oral rehydration solution (Dioralyte) to replace salts.
     - Dietary advice: soft, easily digested foods (e.g., crackers, toast, jam); avoid dairy, meat, fish, eggs while symptomatic.
     - Recommend yogurt (probiotic) as tolerated.
     - Gradual diet advancement: avoid meat/eggs/fish until 48 hours after diarrhea resolves.
     - No antimicrobials prescribed at this time.
   - Follow-up/advice:
     - Seek re-evaluation if diarrhea persists beyond one week, if blood appears in stool, if bowel frequency increases toward 6–8 times/day, or if signs of dehydration develop (may require hospital assessment).

2. Asthma:
   - Assessment or likely diagnosis: Asthma (status unclear).
   - Differential diagnosis: Not applicable based on current transcript.
   - Investigations planned: None documented.
   - Treatment planned: No changes or specific asthma treatment documented; medication use (inhaler named) requires clarification.
